messages:
maria: Hey runtime team — we need a compact QA playbook + raw artifacts for the launch story. Marketing wants: sample latency/cost numbers, warmup protocol, and ~1k raw request/response pairs (anonymized) by EOD Friday. Can you confirm feasibility and a minimal acceptance checklist? @sam

sam: Quick note: we can prioritize a focused smoke + prioritized samplepack. Need exact model name, quantization variants, target seq lengths, and whether embeddings are in scope. GPU calendar is tight Thu-Fri.

maria: Model: redwood-13B-v1 (fp16) + quantized int8 and awq variants. Focus on generation only (no embeddings). Target sequences: 32, 128, 1024. Acceptable: 1k total across slices (not per slice) — marketing will pick 100 samples per seq-length slice for slides.

sam: OK. Suggestion: run a 100-sample smoke across each seq-length on all three variants first (300 total) to validate correctness and warmup. If smoke looks good, we'll ramp to 1k with random sampling. Acceptance checklist I propose:
- No OOMs across variants
- 95th pct latency within SLO (we'll put SLO number after warmup)
- Token-level cost delta logged per request
- Raw request/response JSON + trace ID present

deepa: For slides we also need a short note about methodology: how warmup was done, batching config, and any fallback/rollout behavior. Can you include a one-paragraph writeup?

sam: Yes. We'll include a 3-bullet methodology snippet and the exact run commands. Example run command for smoke (internal):
```bash
./run_bench --model redwood-13B-v1 --variant int8 --seq 128 --samples 100 --tag marketing_launch_2026
```
We'll also attach the raw traces bucket path.

chris: Heads up: if you want KV cache reuse or prefix caching enabled for 1k runs, we'll need to schedule on the dedicated bench queue. Otherwise runs may be preempted. Which do you prefer?

maria: Dedicated queue preferred if it doesn't add >24h to delivery. We care more about reproducibility than hitting the earliest possible time.

sam: Understood. I can reserve a 4-hour window on the dedicated queue tomorrow evening. We can finish smoke there and, if green, continue the full sweep within the reserved window and a follow-up block the next day.

maria: Great. Also include a minimal privacy scrub step — marketing can't get raw user data. Anonymize prompt tokens and remove any PII from responses.

sam: We'll run the anonymizer before handing over artifacts. Expected outputs:
- artifacts/marketing_launch_2026/summary.csv (latencies, costs, percentiles)
- artifacts/marketing_launch_2026/raw_samples.ndjson (anonymized)
- artifacts/marketing_launch_2026/methodology.md
- run_manifest.txt (commands + commit hash + seed)

deepa: Can you also add the seed(s) used for deterministic sampling and a short note about randomization method? Slides will call that out.

sam: Yep — seeds included in run_manifest. Also note: int8 and awq have slightly different tokenization timing; we'll add a note to methodology and a small delta table.

maria: Timeline constraints — marketing needs the 100-sample per-slice screenshots and summary numbers for the deck by 72 hours. Is that doable?

sam: If we start the smoke tonight on the dedicated queue, we can get the 300-sample smoke + screenshots in ~18 hours. The full 1k sweep (with anonymization + packaging) will be ready in ~72 hours. I can escalate if resource conflicts show up.

runbot: deploy-scheduler: reservation created on dedicated-bench (slot id: bench-2026-09) for 4h starting 3743220000.

chris: I'll monitor the slot and ping if any preemptions. Also please attach the exact batch sizes and concurrency used — those affect cost numbers significantly.

sam: Will include batching/concurrency matrix and a small sensitivity table (batch sizes: 1, 4, 8; concurrency: 1-4). Anything else?

maria: One last thing — we want a single-line marketing-safe claim we can paste into the PR: short, conservative, and reproducible. If you can propose a sentence after you see the final numbers, we'll sign off. Thanks team. :pray:

sam: Sounds good. I'll post the smoke artifacts link here when ready and attach the run_manifest.

maria: Thank you all — appreciate the quick turn. :rocket:
